import pandas as pd

# List all source CSV file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_8.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and their types (for reference)
target_columns = [
    'average_salary',  # string
    'city_state',      # string
    'company_id',      # integer
    'company_info',    # string (actually list of tuples as string)
    'company_name',    # string
    'company_rating',  # float
    'country_name',    # string
    'job_desc',        # string
    'job_title',       # string
    'post_date'        # string
]

# Step 1: Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
# Use index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Check schemas of all source tables
# According to the prompt, all source tables have exactly the same schema as the target table.
# So we can safely concatenate (union) all source tables.

# Step 3: Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 4: Ensure the combined DataFrame columns are exactly as target schema and in the same order
# Some source columns might have different types, so we enforce types and formatting as needed.

# Convert company_id to integer (some might be float due to NaNs, so convert carefully)
# We will convert company_id to Int64 dtype (nullable integer) to preserve NaNs if any
combined_df['company_id'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['company_id'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Convert company_rating to float
combined_df['company_rating'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['company_rating'], errors='coerce')

# Convert average_salary to string, preserving NaNs as NaN (will be saved as empty in CSV)
combined_df['average_salary'] = combined_df['average_salary'].astype('string')

# Convert all other columns to string type (as target expects string for most)
for col in ['city_state', 'company_info', 'company_name', 'country_name', 'job_desc', 'job_title', 'post_date']:
    combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Step 6: Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/training_8.csv",
]

dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# UNION all source tables (all have the same schema)
df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Group by the primary key columns of the target table:
# According to FD and hints, primary key is ['company_info', 'post_date']
# But company_info is complex and also city_state and company_id are leftmost and unique enough
# Use group by on [city_state, company_id, company_info, post_date] to ensure uniqueness and match target keys

# Define aggregation functions:
# For average_salary, company_name, company_rating, country_name, job_desc, job_title:
# Use first() to pick one value per group (assuming no conflicts)
agg_dict = {
    'average_salary': 'first',
    'company_name': 'first',
    'company_rating': 'first',
    'country_name': 'first',
    'job_desc': 'first',
    'job_title': 'first'
}

# Perform groupby and aggregation
grouped = df.groupby(['city_state', 'company_id', 'company_info', 'post_date'], dropna=False, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[['average_salary', 'city_state', 'company_id', 'company_info', 'company_name', 'company_rating', 'country_name', 'job_desc', 'job_title', 'post_date']]

# Write output CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_6/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
